scope: Disposable release-gate OAuth seeding order; application authentication and SQLite policies unchanged

actualLocalProtocol.scope: Local seed-order protocol using unchanged source compiled with shipping external-package settings and an isolated controlled production dependency closure refreshed from verified public SDK/workspace builds
checks: Real controlled OAuth challenge/callback seeds the owned SQLite volume before any shipping writer starts
Unmodified production main accepts the callback-issued GitHub session while refusing anonymous and password/setup authentication
A second concurrent fixture writer is still refused by the unchanged exclusive SQLite lock
The actual shipping API persists project, document, discussion and accepted ADR and refuses stale writes
The same callback-issued session and exact document/chat/ADR persist across a real shipping process restart
limitations: This is an actual local dependency-closure/container protocol probe, not a freshly built complete release image.
CI must separately run the full release image and all original model/browser gates.

The local protocol uses the existing controlled production dependency closure refreshed with verified public Connect/Auth dependencies and current built workspace packages. It is not a freshly built complete release image.
The complete CI image gate must still run its unchanged offline model, CPU-affinity, native T3, browser and production-refusal checks.
The seeded identity uses a controlled provider through the real OAuth state/PKCE/browser-binding callback; this does not establish live GitHub account login.
